So the knob is at columns 23-26 (bbSS: b on the left, S on the right — V-left orientation). Wait, knobpos returned 26 (the rightmost b/S column). The knob is at columns 23-26.
Why did it stop there? The beam: the left portion (columns 17-22) is 2 rows tall (rows 19-20), the right portion (columns 23-38) is 4 rows tall (rows 19-22). The knob is 4 rows tall. So the black step is blocking the knob! The knob can only slide on the 4-row-tall portion (columns 23-38), i.e., positions 23-26, 27-30, 31-34, 35-38, and outside at 39-42.

So the black step is a wall. Then what's the purpose of the left frame? The frame is at columns 12-16, with a 4x4 sky interior at rows 18-21. Hmm.
Wait — maybe the knob has to drop down: if the knob is at columns 23-26 (leftmost) and you press DOWN, the knob drops 2 rows (rows 21-24) and can then slide left over the step? Let's test: at columns 23-26, press DOWN.
Actually, the black step is at rows 21-22, columns 17-22. If the knob drops to rows 21-24 at columns 23-26, it's still to the right of the step. Then LEFT → columns 19-22, rows 21-24: the top 2 rows (rows 21-22) overlap with the black step (columns 19-22, rows 21-22). Blocked again?
Hmm. Unless the knob drops further, or the step is passable from below.
Or maybe the knob has to be rotated: H-bottom (blue at the bottom) → the blue bar is at rows 21-22. If the knob is at columns 19-22 with the blue bar at rows 21-22, the blue bar exactly covers the black step region (columns 19-22 ⊂ 17-22)! Maybe the blue bar "fills" the black hole!
The black step is 6 wide (columns 17-22), the blue bar is 4 wide (columns 19-22 or 17-20). Close but not an exact match.
Let's test: at columns 23-26, press DOWN and see if the knob drops.
